_comment: THE PLAN FIELD MODEL — what a plan entry and a plan folder may carry, what
kind each field is, and which of them owe a second language. The companion
to plan-order/stages.json: that file is the single source for a plan's
ORDER vocabulary, this one for its FIELD vocabulary.
WHY IT EXISTS. The model was written down in four places and none of them
could see the others: the ENTRY_NOTES / FOLDER_NOTES maps inside the Field
Legend page (contents/docs/plan-fields.html), `_BILINGUAL_BASES` inside
plan_data_check, and a sentence naming the bases in each of the `bilingual`
shelf library and 日程 Agenda's plan/translate.py. Two independent misses
followed, both found on 2026-08-25:
· `detail` was undocumented on the tree side. The Legend page derives its
field NAMES from live data and flags any it has no note for — a good
design, but it reads ONE plan, site-entries.yaml, because a deployed
site can only fetch the plans deployed beside it. `detail` is used by
origin-entries.yaml, which is a console plan and never ships there. So
the drift banner could not see the drift, and the field the plan pages
render a whole disclosure for had no row in its own legend.
· plan_data_check's first bilingual audit required BOTH languages of
`desc` and `detail`, which are mono by default — the Legend page had
said so in prose since it was written. The check reported a settled
choice as a gap because it could not read the rule it was enforcing.
WHAT IS DERIVED AND WHAT IS DECLARED, unchanged by this file. Which fields
are PRESENT in a given plan is a fact, and the Legend page keeps deriving
it from the data. What a field MEANS, what kind it is, and whether it owes
a second language are decisions, and decisions live here. The page still
flags a live field with no entry in this file — the drift check now has
something cross-language to check against.
both_languages: 'required' — an audit failure to write only one side;
'optional' — mono is a normal state (you may translate it, you are not owed
a second side). Absent on a field that is not bilingual at all.
legacy_bases: older BASE names a reader still accepts, i.e. ones that also
take the _en / _zh / _raw suffixes. Not the same thing as the older
ASYMMETRIC pairs (bare `text`=English with bare `zh`=Chinese; bare
`description` with `description_zh`), which are not bases at all and are
named in the notes below instead — listing them here produced a scanner
hunting for `zh_en:`. The `bilingual` shelf library owns the trio model and
the dual-read rule; this only records which bases wore which older names.
Array order IS display order — the Legend page renders rows in the order
they appear here, so there is no separate index to keep in step.
JSON, and in 引擎 Engines with a .public marker, for stages.json's reasons:
readers in two languages (the Legend page fetches it in the browser;
plan_data_check json.loads it in Python), no dependency in either, and the
marker is what carries it to the deployed site beside the page that reads
it.

entry.note: when the entry is due: a roadmap version token (v1.0, p0.3 — the website's plans) or a rung of the named ladder (see plan-order/stages.json). Absent means no stage chosen.
the entry's descriptive line — its title. The one field owed both languages. Older asymmetric pair: bare `text` (English) with bare `zh` (Chinese).
optional short title, bold above the line (added incrementally)
long body, hidden until the entry row is clicked (plan-renderer.js toggleDetail). Mono by default — only detail_en unless you translate it.

folder.note: anchor (section only), e.g. dev-design — set once, never renamed
folder / subgroup heading (monolingual — a structural label, not prose)
blurb under the folder heading. Mono by default. Older asymmetric pair: bare `description` (English) with `description_zh`.
